What is the atomic number of Cadmium?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
What is the atomic number of Lead?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.
In what year was Srinivasa Ramanujan born?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Euler's formula discovered?
Euler's formula: The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
COBOL: CODASYL. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Propofol: Pfizer. Propofol is the active component of an intravenous anesthetic used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia.
Boxer (dog breed): German Empire. The Boxer is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
Who is credited with discovering Special relativity?
Special relativity: Albert Einstein. In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon dioxide?
Carbon dioxide: Jan Baptist van Helmont. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Who is credited with discovering Calcium?
Calcium: Humphry Davy. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
First added to the DSM in 1980 and diagnosed in women twice as often as men, this condition describes an intense, maladaptive reaction to a stressful life event — what is it?
Adjustment disorder is a mental disorder defined by a maladaptive response to a psychosocial stressor.
This cation forms when a proton attaches to ammonia, giving living organisms a vital source of nitrogen — what ion is it?
Ammonium is a modified form of ammonia that has an extra hydrogen atom.
Linked to smoking, high blood pressure and older age, this silent widening of the body's main artery to over 1.5 times normal size can suddenly rupture with severe abdominal pain — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm is an enlargement (dilatation) of the aorta to greater than 1.5 times normal size.
Originally built by Hawker Siddeley and still produced under license in India today, this subsonic British trainer aircraft equips the Red Arrows aerobatic team — which jet?
BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.
Ranging from fingerprints and iris scans to typing rhythm and the way someone walks, these measurable human traits are used for identification and surveillance — what's the general term for them?
Biometrics are body measurements and calculations related to human characteristics and features.
Named in a 2018 New York Times essay by Bari Weiss as part of the 'intellectual dark web,' this former evolutionary biology professor left academia after 2017 campus protests — who is he?
Bret Weinstein (born February 21, 1969) is an American podcaster, author, and former professor of evolutionary biology.

Ranging from 9 to 20 centimeters long and known on the Italian mainland by a slightly different name, this Sicilian pastry features a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with a sweet ricotta cream — which pastry?
Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
First flown in 1998, this Chinese-built multirole combat aircraft features a delta wing and canard design and is nicknamed "Vigorous Dragon" — which fighter jet is it?

Chengdu J-10 (pinyin: Jian-Shi), also known as Menglong (pinyin: Menglong; lit. 'Vigorous Dragon'), is a Chinese medium-weight, single-engine, multirole combat aircraft with a delta wing and canard design.
Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.
This blood-feeding parasitic insect usually lives in human pubic hair and is thought to have diverged from a closely related gorilla parasite roughly 3.3 million years ago — what is it?
Crab louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.

This condition's four subtypes include one caused by kidneys that don't respond to a hormone called vasopressin and another linked to excessive fluid intake from a damaged thirst mechanism — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.
What common name covers a diverse family of marine ray-finned fish in the order Perciformes, most belonging to the genera Epinephelus or Mycteroperca?
Grouper are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.

Ranging from mild headaches and poor balance to severe confusion and seizures, this low-blood-sodium condition can be triggered by causes as varied as vomiting, diuretics, or overhydration — what's it called?
Hyponatremia is a low concentration of sodium in the blood. It is generally defined as a sodium concentration of less than 135 mmol/L (135 mEq/L), with severe hyponatremia being below 120 mEq/L.
This Mexican neurophysiologist studied shamanism, meditation, and telepathy through the scientific method, writing more than 50 books before vanishing in December 1994 — who is he?
Jacobo Grinberg (born Mexico City in 1946) was a Mexican neurophysiologist and psychologist.

This 20th-century Peruvian writer of mestizo descent composed novels, poems, and stories in both Spanish and Quechua, and even coined a new literary idiom to render Indigenous perspective more authentically — who is he?
José María Arguedas (Spanish) was a Peruvian novelist, poet, and anthropologist.
Depicted as the goddess Minerva, this Italian physicist became the first woman with a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher. Who was she?
Laura Bassi (29 October 1711 - 20 February 1778) was an Italian physicist and academic.
Prized as one of the most profitable seafood commodities in the coastal waters where it's caught, this clawed crustacean spends its life in crevices and burrows on the sea floor - which creature?
Lobster are malacostracan decapod crustaceans of the family Nephropidae or its synonym Homaridae.
Its bell-shaped flowers give way to yellow or orange berries, but this nightshade genus is better known by the folkloric root that inspired countless myths and superstitions — which genus?
Mandragora (genus) is a plant genus belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
First synthesized in 2003 by Russian and American scientists at Dubna, this synthetic element — atomic number 115 — was named in 2016 for the oblast around its birthplace — what is it?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Found across North America, Europe, North Africa, and Asia, this three-stage amphibian passes through an aquatic larval phase and a land-dwelling 'eft' stage before adulthood — what is it?
Newt is a salamander in the subfamily Pleurodelinae.

Physicians in this medical specialty diagnose and surgically treat eye disorders — and can often spot signs of diseases elsewhere in the body just by examining a patient's eyes — what specialty is it?
Ophthalmology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of eye diseases and disorders.
This British theoretical physicist, one of the founders of quantum mechanics, coined the term 'quantum electrodynamics' and shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Paul Dirac (dih-RAK; 8 August 1902 - 20 October 1984) was a British theoretical physicist who is considered to be one of the founders of quantum mechanics.
With a musty odor like freshly cut hay, this toxic colorless gas is the double acyl-chloride cousin of carbonic acid, and it saw grim use as a chemical weapon in World War I. Name the compound?
Phosgene is an organic chemical compound with the formula COCl2.
This spiny rodent actually comes in two unrelated varieties, an Old World family and a New World family, whose lookalike coats of keratin quills evolved independently — what animal is it?
Porcupine are large rodents with coats of sharp spines, or quills, that protect them against predators.
This yellow-white fluid forms at sites of infection and inflammation — when trapped in tissue it's called an abscess, and near the skin's surface a pimple — name the substance?
Pus is an exudate, typically white-yellow, yellow, or yellow-brown, formed at the site of inflammation during infections, regardless of cause.
Also known as vitamin B2, this nutrient builds two key coenzymes for energy metabolism and may, taken orally, cut down on migraine headaches in adults — what is it?
Riboflavin is a vitamin found in food and sold as a dietary supplement.

This volatile, colorless, and odorless nerve agent is so potent a chemical weapon that inhaling a lethal dose can cause death from respiratory paralysis within one to ten minutes — what's the compound called?
Sarin (NATO designation GB short for G-series, B) is an extremely toxic organophosphorus compound that has been often used as a chemical weapon due to its extreme potency as a nerve agent.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.

Distinguished from relatives in its conifer family by four-sided needles attached singly to small peg-like structures on the twigs, this genus of about 37 evergreen tree species thrives across the Northern Hemisphere's boreal forests — what's the tree?

Spruce is a tree of the genus Picea, a genus of some 37 species of coniferous evergreen trees in the family Pinaceae, found in the northern temperate and boreal (taiga) regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
Serving as prime minister seven separate times before becoming president from 1993 to 2000, this Turkish statesman led two different political parties across his long career — who was he?
Süleyman Demirel (1 November 1924 - 17 June 2015) was a Turkish politician, engineer, and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1993 to 2000.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Developed by Microsoft as open-source software, this programming language adds optional static typing to JavaScript and transpiles back into it — name the language?
TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.

This teenage prodigy's work on solvable polynomials helped birth what's now called group theory, and his fiery Republican politics landed him in prison before a fatal duel ended his life at 20 — who was he?
Évariste Galois (25 October 1811 - 31 May 1832) was a French mathematician and political activist.
Recognizable by its black-and-white striped legs and a lyre-shaped marking on its thorax, this mosquito native to North Africa spreads dengue and yellow fever worldwide — what is it?
Aedes aegypti: Species of mosquito. The mosquito can be recognized by black and white markings on its legs and a marking in the form of a lyre on the upper surface of its thorax.
This German polar researcher proposed in 1912 that the continents were slowly drifting apart, a theory mainstream geology only accepted decades later thanks to palaeomagnetism — who was he?
Alfred Wegener: German climatologist and geophysicist (1880–1930)

Inspired by Ørsted's 1820 discovery that current creates a magnetic field, this principle relating a magnetic field's circulation to the current passing through a loop was later generalized by Maxwell with a displacement current term — which physics principle?
Ampère's circuital law: Concept in classical electromagnetism.

A political economy professor turned finance minister after a 1926 coup, this Portuguese dictator ruled his corporatist 'New State' from 1932 until 1968, in one of modern Europe's longest authoritarian regimes — who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar: Prime Minister of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.

Also known by a folksy nickname, this small North American tree produces a custard-textured fruit tasting like banana or pineapple — despite containing a neurotoxin elsewhere in the plant. What species is it?
Asimina triloba: Species of tree. Asimina triloba, the American papaw, pawpaw, paw paw, or paw-paw, among many regional names, is a species of small deciduous tree.
This fig tree spreads outward indefinitely by growing extra trunks from its own prop roots, and its most famous species is the national tree of India — what is it?

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
Once used in Italy for hunting large game and herding cattle, this mastiff breed today mostly serves as a guard dog or companion — which breed?
Cane Corso: Italian breed of mastiff. It is usually kept as a companion dog or guard dog; it may also be used to protect livestock.
Marked by patients who may lie motionless for days or repeat purposeless movements, this neuropsychiatric syndrome often responds to benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy — which condition?
Domesticated from the red junglefowl roughly 8,000 years ago, this bird now numbers over 26 billion worldwide, more than any other domesticated species — what is it?
Chicken: Domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl. The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Found in birds, reptiles, amphibians, and egg-laying mammals like the platypus, which single all-purpose body opening handles digestion, reproduction, and waste?
The heaviest songbird on Earth and the most widely distributed of all the corvids, this all-black passerine averages 25 inches long across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Common raven: Large, black species of passerine bird.
This interdisciplinary field draws on sociology, psychology, and law to study crime, deviant behavior, and the workings of the justice system — what is it called?
Criminology: Field of studies related to crimes.
At just 37 this American biologist won a 1975 Nobel for discovering reverse transcriptase, later running Caltech and founding the Whitehead Institute — who is he?
David Baltimore: American biologist and Nobel laureate (1938–2025)
These warmblooded reptiles ruled the land for the whole Mesozoic, and one feathered lineage of theirs survived the extinction 66 million years ago as today's birds — what group is this?
Dinosaur: Clade of reptiles. Since then, mounted fossil dinosaur skeletons have been major attractions at museums worldwide, and dinosaurs have become an enduring part of popular culture.
Belonging to the phylum Annelida and often called a 'nightcrawler' by anglers, this segmented soil-dweller is the classic bait fished from underground burrows — which invertebrate?
Continuous with the outer nuclear membrane and absent from red blood cells, this organelle comes in rough and smooth forms and handles protein folding — what is it?
Endoplasmic reticulum: Cell organelle that processes proteins.
Recognizable by its striking yellow-and-azure plumage, this small European songbird nests in tree holes and can acrobatically hang upside-down from branch tips — which bird?
Eurasian blue tit: Species of bird. The Eurasian blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) is a small passerine bird in the tit family, Paridae.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
A pungent colorless gas churned out at 26 million tons a year, it's used to make resins and, in a roughly 37% solution, to preserve tissue samples in labs — what is it?

Marked by heartburn, regurgitation, and even dental corrosion from stomach acid creeping back up the digestive tract, this chronic condition can, if untreated, lead to esophageal stricture or Barrett's esophagus — what is it?
Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Flow of stomach contents into the esophagus.
The most abundant free amino acid in human blood, this one is named after the compound found in gluten and is coded for by the codons CAA and CAG — what is it?
Glutamine: Amino acid. Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an α-amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.

Beginning as weakness in the feet and hands before spreading upward, this rapid-onset autoimmune condition attacks the peripheral nervous system and can require a ventilator in about 15% of cases — which disorder is this?
Guillain–Barré syndrome: Autoimmune disease. Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rapid-onset muscle weakness caused by the immune system damaging the peripheral nervous system.
Nicknamed a 'strawberry mark' in infants, this usually benign vascular tumor tends to grow for about a year before gradually shrinking — what is it?
Hemangioma: Vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera, some 158 species of this fragrant plant attract hummingbirds in North America — what is it?

Defined as a blood sodium level below 135 millimoles per liter, this condition can arise from drinking excessive water — or even too much beer — and in severe cases causes seizures or coma — what is it?
Hyponatremia: Low sodium concentration in the blood.

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.
Serving as special adviser to the UN Secretary-General from 2002 to 2018, which Columbia University economist co-founded a nonprofit dedicated to ending extreme poverty?
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.

Credited as a 'Father of Cinematography,' this French artist filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888 — then vanished without a trace two years later, and his work never shaped commercial cinema. Who was he?
Louis Le Prince: French motion-picture pioneer (1841–1890s)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.
Home to the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and central chest lymph nodes, this compartment of the thoracic cavity sits between the lungs — what's it called?
Mediastinum: Central part of the thoracic cavity. The mediastinum (from Medieval Latin: mediastinus, lit. 'midway';pl.: mediastina) is the central compartment of the thoracic cavity.
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)

There's a large introduced population of this small carnivorous mammal in Hawaii, though its family — split into the Herpestinae and Mungotinae — is native to southern Europe, Africa, and Asia — what animal is it?

Mongoose: Family of mammals in Africa and Asia. The Herpestinae comprises 23 living species that are native to southern Europe, Africa and Asia, whereas the Mungotinae comprises 11 species native to Africa.
Named for its resemblance to a tiny mouse's ear, this flowering plant genus is known in the Northern Hemisphere by a romantic common name and is Alaska's official flower — what is it?
Myosotis: Genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae.
This synthetic element 113 was claimed by both a Russian-American team at Dubna and, in 2004, a Japanese team at Riken. What's its name?
Nihonium: Chemical element with atomic number 113 (Nh)

This family of 138 primate species — including baboons, macaques, and mandrills — split off from a separate lineage of primates some 45 to 55 million years ago, yet is the closer kin to apes of the two — which family?
Old World monkey: Family of mammals. Old World monkey genera include baboons (genus Papio), red colobus (genus Piliocolobus), and macaques (genus Macaca).
A pale-blue gas with a chlorine-like pungent odour, this unstable three-atom cousin of oxygen forms by UV light and electrical discharges and shields us high in the stratosphere — what is it?
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Home to cereal crops like wheat, rice, and maize as well as bamboo, this is the fifth-largest plant family on Earth — what is it called?
Poaceae: Family of flowering plants commonly known as grasses.

Detected by receptors in your muscles, tendons, and joints, this sense tells your brain where your body is in space, working alongside vision and balance to keep you upright and coordinated — what's it called?
Proprioception: Sense of self-movement, force, and body position.
Found in notable amounts in capers, red onions, and kale, this bitter-tasting plant flavonol is a popular ingredient in dietary supplements — what compound?
Quercetin: Chemical compound. It is found in many fruits, vegetables, leaves, seeds, and grains; capers, red onions, and kale are common foods containing appreciable amounts of it.

Found in fish, dairy, and meat, this fat-soluble vitamin A derivative is prescribed for xerophthalmia and used topically in anti-wrinkle skincare — but too much during pregnancy can harm the fetus. What is it?
Once used by German butchers to herd cattle and pull meat carts to market, this mastiff-type breed now works as a search-and-rescue and police dog — which breed?
Rottweiler: Large German dog breed. The Rottweiler (UK also, German: [ˈʁɔtvaɪ̯lɐ]) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.

Discovered in 1879 via spectral analysis of Scandinavian minerals, this silvery-white rare-earth element with atomic number 21 wasn't isolated in metallic form until 1937, and today it's prized for strengthening aluminum alloys — which element?
Scandium: Chemical element with atomic number 21 (Sc)
Built with a ribless cartilage skeleton, skin-covering dermal denticles and five to seven gill slits per side, these fish first appeared back in the Devonian — what are they?
With the formula Na2SO4, this white, water-soluble compound is produced at six million tonnes a year and used as a filler in powdered laundry detergent — which compound?

Sodium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula Na2SO4. Sodium sulfate (also known as sodium sulphate or sulfate of soda) is the inorganic compound with formula Na2SO4 as well as several related hydrates.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
Fully aquatic marine mammals split into baleen and toothed kinds, their nearest land relatives are surprisingly the hippos, from which they diverged some 54 million years ago. What are they?
Whale: Informal group of large marine mammals.
These striped African equines share their genus with horses and asses, and the leading theory says their patterns evolved mainly to deter biting flies — what are they?
Zebra: Striped animal in the equid family.
What is the chemical symbol for bohrium?
The symbol for bohrium is Bh. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
The symbol for neon is Ne. Neon is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ne and the atomic number 10.

Which of these is a comedian?
Peter Serafinowicz is a comedian. Peter Szymon Serafinowicz ( SERR-ə-FIN-oh-witch; Polish: [sɛrafʲiˈnɔvʲit͡ʂ]; born 10 July 1972) is an English actor, comedian and writer.
In what year was Jesse Plemons born?
Jesse Plemons (born April 2, 1988) is an American actor.
In what year was Blake Lively born?
Blake Lively: Blake Ellender Brown (born August 25, 1987), known professionally as Blake Lively, is an American actress and entrepreneur.
In what year was Pete Davidson born?
Pete Davidson: Peter Michael Davidson (born November 16, 1993) is an American comedian, actor, and writer.
In what year was Nick Jonas born?
Nick Jonas: Nicholas Jerry Jonas (born September 16, 1992) is an American singer, songwriter, musician and actor.
In what year was Reba McEntire born?
Reba McEntire: Reba Nell McEntire ( REE-bə MAK-in-tire; born March 28, 1955), or simply Reba, is an American country singer and actress.
In what year was Riley Keough born?
Riley Keough: Danielle Riley Keough ( KEE-oh; born May 29, 1989) is an American actress.
In what year was Penn Badgley born?
Penn Badgley: Penn Dayton Badgley (born November 1, 1986) is an American actor and producer.
In what year was Nicole Kidman born?
Nicole Kidman: Nicole Mary Kidman (born 20 June 1967) is an Australian-American actress and producer.
